topics.label: Lecture framing and objectives for cancer causation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, situates the lecture in the course, and sets out its aims before the substantive material begins.

topics.label: Cancer as clonal evolution shaped by mutations and context
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics frame cancer as the selection and expansion of cells with consequential mutations, shaped by the conditions and predispositions that affect that process.

topics.label: Weighing environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: They consider how environmental exposures may contribute to cancer and how that contribution is weighed against chance and inherited susceptibility using population-level patterns.

topics.label: Infectious contributions to cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: They show how infections can contribute to cancer, moving from pathogen-associated cancers generally to the EBV and malaria context of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: DNA damage from noninfectious environmental exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how noninfectious environmental exposures can produce DNA lesions and mutations through direct damage or through activation and oxidative processes.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and context-dependent susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how carcinogenesis depends not just on DNA mutation but also on conditions that help damaged cells emerge, while the final subtopic consolidates the mechanisms discussed.

topics.label: Mutational signatures for tracing carcinogen exposure
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how patterns of mutations in cancer genomes can provide evidence of exposure to particular carcinogens.

topics.label: Epidemiological assessment of carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how population studies, exposure biomarkers, and biobanks can be used to investigate links between exposures and cancer.

topics.label: Experimental assays of carcinogenic potential
topics.groupedBecause: Both subtopics describe experimental tests for carcinogenic or mutagenic potential and explain why their results have limitations.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This final subtopic recaps the difficulty of identifying carcinogens and closes by framing exposure decisions as a balance of risks and benefits.
